data.one_liner: Unifies local storage packages under a single object-oriented JSON caching interface.
data.what_it_does: JsonCache is an object-oriented package that provides a uniform interface for caching user data locally in JSON format. It acts as a layer on top of various storage packages like SharedPreferences, Hive, LocalStorage, and FlutterSecureStorage.
use_when: You want to abstract your local storage layer behind a unified interface.
You need to cache Map data easily or store simple values with boolean placeholders.
You want to combine in-memory caching with persistent local storage seamlessly.
avoid_when: You need a full relational database with complex querying capabilities.
You require automatic code-generation for models and JSON serialization.
strengths: Provides a clean, uniform interface over multiple local storage backends.
Includes thread-safe in-memory caching and diagnostic wrappers.
Enables easy unit testing by depending on interfaces rather than concrete implementations.
weaknesses: Limited to JSON-encodable map structures and specific primitive wrappers.
Relies on underlying third-party storage packages which must be independently configured.
data.setup_notes: Requires initializing the chosen underlying storage package (e.g., SharedPreferences, Hive) before wrapping it with JsonCache.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need simple key-value storage and do not want an abstraction layer over multiple backends.

alternatives.name: flutter_secure_storage
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically need encrypted storage without a generic JSON caching layer.

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you need a full SQL relational database instead of simple JSON key-value caching.
